papers.title: An Error Analysis of Flow Matching for Deep Generative Modeling
papers.decision_reason: This is a direct Euclidean flow-matching error-analysis baseline for the seed profile's learned-velocity and Wasserstein convergence questions. It is likely to yield reusable proof patterns for epsilon-accurate velocity fields and W2 sampling guarantees.
papers.notes: Read before or alongside the seed Wasserstein proof to compare assumptions and proof decompositions.

papers.title: Error Bounds for Flow Matching Methods
papers.decision_reason: This is a core flow-matching error-bound paper and should anchor the general proof framework before reading geometric extensions. It likely contains reusable approximation-error-to-sampling-error arguments.
papers.notes: High value for paper-to-skill extraction because it is proof-centered and close to the seed assumptions.

papers.title: Flow Matching on General Geometries
papers.decision_reason: This is the foundational Riemannian/geometric flow matching method paper. Even if it is less proof-heavy on sampling rates, it is essential for definitions, geometry, and positioning.
papers.notes: Use it to map definitions and method lineage before extracting proof-patterns from later RFM theory papers.

papers.title: Geometry-Grounded Flow Matching on Compact Manifolds
papers.decision_reason: This is very close to the Riemannian TV seed paper but emphasizes Wasserstein and end-to-end compact-manifold guarantees. It is a strong candidate for cross-paper synthesis with the seed RFM paper.
papers.notes: Potentially high-value for extracting geometric FM proof patterns.

papers.title: Lipschitz regularity in Flow Matching and Diffusion Models: sharp sampling rates and functional inequalities
papers.decision_reason: This paper directly targets the seed profile's bottleneck around velocity-field Lipschitz regularity, terminal-time behavior, and discretization rates. It is likely harder to read but has the highest innovation potential.
papers.notes: Read for innovation and possible weakening/sharpening of regularity assumptions.

papers.title: Gauge Flow Matching: Efficient Constrained Generative Modeling over General Convex Set and Beyond
papers.decision_reason: This is the strongest alternative constrained-domain method to mirror/reflected flow matching. It is important for positioning and may suggest a different transformation-based route for constrained FM.
papers.notes: Read to compare gauge maps with regularized mirror maps.

papers.title: Mirror Diffusion Models for Constrained and Watermarked Generation
papers.decision_reason: This is essential mirror-map constrained-generation background, but it is diffusion-focused rather than flow-matching error analysis. It should be read for method lineage and assumptions.
papers.notes: Useful context before writing related-work or comparing constrained generation approaches.

papers.title: Reflected Flow Matching
papers.decision_reason: This paper addresses the same constrained-domain problem with reflection rather than mirror maps or gauge maps. It is important for method comparison, though likely less central for proof-pattern extraction.
papers.notes: Read after Gauge Flow Matching unless the focus shifts toward constraint-satisfaction mechanisms.

papers.title: On the Convergence and Straightness of Rectified Flow
papers.decision_reason: The straightness abstraction may reframe discretization error as path geometry, which is a promising innovation direction. It is not as directly related as RFM/constrained FM papers, so it belongs in should_read.
papers.notes: Read if the goal is to find new theoretical angles rather than only map related work.

papers.title: The probability flow ODE is provably fast
papers.decision_reason: This adjacent deterministic ODE sampler paper may provide proof techniques for polynomial-time convergence under noncontractive dynamics. It is not flow matching, so read selectively for transferable proof moves.
papers.notes: Skim first; download if the proof architecture looks transferable.

papers.title: Polynomial Convergence of Riemannian Diffusion Models
papers.decision_reason: This is diffusion rather than flow matching, but its Riemannian TV and curvature proof techniques are close to the RFM TV seed. It should be read selectively for proof-method transfer.
papers.notes: Useful for cross-domain proof patterns, especially curvature and TV control.

papers.title: Riemannian Score-Based Generative Modelling
papers.decision_reason: This is important background for manifold generative modeling, but it is less directly aligned with deterministic RFM proof-pattern extraction. Read if related-work context is needed.
papers.notes: Keep as background unless the project expands to diffusion comparisons.

papers.title: Neural Approximate Mirror Maps for Constrained Diffusion Models
papers.decision_reason: Learned mirror maps are conceptually relevant, but this is diffusion-oriented and may not provide immediate sampler-theory proof patterns. Save for later method-design exploration.
papers.notes: Potential future direction if mirror flow matching needs learned transformations.

papers.title: Flow Matching Generalizes Through Discretization Bias
papers.decision_reason: The idea that discretization bias can help generalization is interesting, but it is speculative relative to the seed profile's rigorous geometric sampler guarantees. Keep it as an innovation note.
papers.notes: Do not prioritize unless exploring conceptual reframing of discretization.

papers.title: Generative Modeling with Continuous Flows: Sample Complexity of Flow Matching
papers.decision_reason: This could replace the assumed epsilon-accurate velocity field with sample/optimization complexity, but that is one layer upstream of the current sampler-theory focus.
papers.notes: Save until after core sampler-discretization papers are processed.

papers.title: Are We Really Learning the Score Function? Reinterpreting Diffusion Models Through Wasserstein Gradient Flow Matching
papers.decision_reason: This is a conceptual diffusion reinterpretation and only indirectly related to geometric flow matching error bounds. It is useful only if the project broadens to score-vs-velocity abstractions.
papers.notes: Low priority for the current proof-pattern mining workflow.
